body: Microsoft Flight Simulator cannot train someone to fly a Boeing 737 or an Airbus A320 on its own, but its authentic geography, weather and avionics have made it a popular tool for supplementing flight school at many levels. A home setup lacks the motion feedback and the full flight deck of a certified airline simulator, yet the software's high-fidelity interface, physics, aircraft attributes and environment give users a realistic cockpit atmosphere to learn in.

The simulator models airflow across hundreds of points on the airframe, while third-party add-ons recreate Garmin G1000 glass cockpits, navigation radios and flight management systems down to individual electrical circuits. That combination of system accuracy and little tactile input makes home simulation well suited to instrument flight instruction: student pilots and hobbyists can connect a desktop setup to virtual air traffic control and practise instrument scans and radio calls from home, saving money on aircraft rentals and instructor hours.

Practising at home removes fuel costs, aircraft rental fees and safety hazards, and gives aspiring pilots unlimited chances to grasp ideas in a safe setting. While flying with an instructor, students can repeat a navigation exercise or reset an approach without worrying about running out of time or money on aviation fuel, and a student pilot aiming for the A320 or 737 can learn airline standard operating procedures by practising with high-fidelity add-ons at home.

The physical gap remains real. Real flight controls grow heavier as airspeed increases, and an airline emergency such as an engine failure on a Boeing 737 MAX 8 at takeoff decision speed requires 80 pounds (36 kilograms) of rudder pressure to keep the jet straight, while standard desktop yokes rely on simple springs with constant tension. Pairing force-feedback controls with immersive headsets creates realistic scan patterns and cockpit familiarity, even if light plastic pedals cannot match that heavy resistance. Unguided play can also teach bad habits: casual users may stare at cockpit screens instead of watching outside for traffic and the horizon, as they must in trainers such as the Cessna 172 or Piper Archer. Following real-world checklists and using virtual reality or mixed-reality interfaces that align virtual switches with physical mockups reinforces accurate visual scanning and spatial awareness.

Regulators also draw a firm line. Personal computer hours do not count towards a commercial pilot licence or an airline transport rating, because the Federal Aviation Administration requires certified training devices to have enclosed cockpits, physical switches and tested aerodynamic software. Even so, students who arrive at the airport with established procedural knowledge can spend their paid aircraft hours on handling and manoeuvre practice instead of learning switch layouts. Basic training aircraft and flight instructors can cost up to $200 per hour, while a single upfront purchase of home software allows endless practice without fuel or maintenance fees.

The two aircraft families feel genuinely different inside the simulator. Loading a Boeing 737 Next Generation or 737 MAX add-on puts the user in a traditional flight deck with a centre yoke, physical trim wheels that spin beside the seat, manual control yokes and overhead panels full of toggle switches to operate by hand. Moving to an Airbus A320ceo or A320neo feels like stepping into a digital workstation: a side-mounted joystick, push-button overhead panels and fly-by-wire computers that trim the aircraft automatically and prevent the pilot from banking or pitching too far. Boeing expects pilots to stay hands-on with manual thrust changes and step-by-step checklist routines, while Airbus automates common duties through flight guidance modes and centralised electronic warning screens.

Beyond the cockpit, the simulator's realistic airport layouts and detailed global landscape let users practise in crowded, realistic airspace. Complicated hubs such as New York JFK, London Heathrow or Tokyo Haneda teach standard instrument departure paths, runway markings and complex taxiway layouts, and students can learn how a Boeing and an Airbus differ in cockpit workload during taxi, take-off and climb. A home simulator also works as a safe sandbox for pushing an airliner to its limits: users can try a steep approach, shut off a hydraulic system or start an engine fire at take-off speed to see how the flight computers and control surfaces respond, or load a Boeing 737 MAX or Airbus A320neo to maximum weight, add a strong crosswind and land on a short mountain runway to test brakes and spoilers.

What the screen cannot give is the physical feedback of a real jet: the forceful pushback on the rudder pedals after an engine failure, the heavy airframe shudder before a stall, or actual G-forces pressing the pilot into the seat. A desktop simulator does a good job of displaying warning lights, Master Caution bells and flight manual numbers, and it builds the mental habits that help a pilot spot problems early. Used as a visual sandbox for learning how the systems think, rather than as a substitute for feeling a real aeroplane fly, it turns abstract concepts into something students can see, test and understand in real time.
en.summary: Microsoft Flight Simulator cannot teach anyone to fly a Boeing 737 or Airbus A320 on its own, but its faithful systems, add-on cockpits and virtual air traffic control make it a powerful and cheap supplement to real flight training, within clear physical and regulatory limits.

body: 微軟飛行模擬器（Microsoft Flight Simulator）無法單憑自己教會一個人駕駛波音737或空中巴士A320，但它逼真的地理、氣象與航電系統，已使它成為輔助各階段飛行學校訓練的熱門工具。家用設備缺乏認證航空模擬機的動感回饋與完整駕駛艙，但軟體高度擬真的介面、物理特性、飛機屬性與環境，仍能為使用者營造出真實的駕駛艙氛圍。
模擬器會模擬氣流通過機身數百個點的情形，第三方擴充軟體更能重現Garmin G1000玻璃駕駛艙、導航無線電與飛航管理系統，精細到個別電路。這種系統準確度高、觸覺回饋少的組合，非常適合儀器飛行教學：學員與愛好者可以把桌上型模擬器接上虛擬航管，在家練習儀器掃描與無線電通話，省下飛機租賃與教練費用。
在家練習省去了燃油成本、飛機租賃費與安全風險，讓有志成為飛行員的人有無限次機會在安全的環境中掌握概念。和教練一起飛行時，學員可以重複練習導航科目或重設進場程序，不必擔心航空燃油的時間或金錢耗損；未來想飛A320或737的學員，也能透過高擬真擴充軟體在家學習航空公司的標準作業程序。

物理上的落差仍然真實存在。真實飛機的操縱會隨空速增加而變重，波音737 MAX 8在起飛決斷速度發生發動機失效這類緊急狀況，需要36公斤的方向舵壓力才能讓飛機保持直線，而標準桌上型駕駛盤只靠張力固定的簡單彈簧。力回饋操縱裝置搭配沉浸式頭戴裝置，能營造逼真的掃描模式與駕駛艙熟悉度，即使輕巧的塑膠腳踏板無法重現那種沉重的阻力。缺乏引導的隨意遊玩也可能養成壞習慣：休閒玩家可能只盯著駕駛艙螢幕，而忽略了在塞斯納172或派珀Archer等教練機上必須向外觀察交通狀況與地平線。遵循真實檢查表、使用能讓虛擬開關對上實體模型的虛擬實境或混合實境介面，有助於強化正確的目視掃描與空間感。
法規也畫出明確界線。個人電腦的時數不能計入商用飛行員執照或航線運輸駕駛員資格，因為美國聯邦航空總署要求認證訓練設備具備封閉式駕駛艙、實體開關與經過測試的空氣動力軟體。即便如此，帶著既有程序知識到機場的學員，可以把付費的飛機時數花在操縱與機動練習上，而不必從找開關學起。基礎教練機與飛行教練每小時費用可達200美元，而家用軟體一次買斷後可無限練習，不必再付燃油或維護費用。

兩個機型家族在模擬器裡的手感確實不同。載入波音737次世代或737 MAX擴充軟體，會進入傳統駕駛艙：中央駕駛盤、座位旁會轉動的實體配平輪、手動操縱桿，以及滿是撥動開關、需要手動操作的頭頂面板。換到空中巴士A320ceo或A320neo，則像走進數位工作站：側置操縱桿、按鈕式頭頂面板，以及會自動配平、防止飛行員過度轉彎或俯仰的線傳飛控電腦。波音要求飛行員以手動推力變化與逐步檢查表親力親為，空中巴士則透過飛航指引模式與集中式電子警告螢幕自動處理許多例行工作。

駕駛艙之外，模擬器逼真的機場布局與精細的全球地景，讓使用者能在擁擠而真實的空域中練習。紐約甘迺迪、倫敦希斯洛或東京羽田等複雜樞紐，可以學到標準儀器離場航路、跑道標線與複雜滑行道布局，學員也能體會波音與空中巴士在滑行、起飛與爬升階段的駕駛艙工作負荷有何不同。家用模擬器也是安全的試驗場，可以把客機推到極限：嘗試陡峭進場、關掉液壓系統，或在起飛速度引發發動機起火，觀察飛航電腦與操縱面如何反應；也可以把波音737 MAX或空中巴士A320neo載到最大重量，加上強烈側風，降落在短小的山區跑道上測試煞車與擾流板。
螢幕給不了的是真實噴射機的身體回饋：發動機失效後方向舵踏板傳來的強力反推、失速前機身沉重的震動，或是真正把飛行員壓進座椅的G力。桌上型模擬器在顯示警告燈、主警告鈴聲與飛行手冊數據方面表現出色，也能培養及早發現問題的心理習慣。把它當作學習系統如何思考的視覺沙盒，而不是感受真實飛機飛行的替代品，它就能把抽象概念變成學員可以即時看見、測試與理解的東西。
zh.summary: 微軟飛行模擬器無法單憑自己教會人駕駛波音737或空中巴士A320，但它擬真的系統、擴充駕駛艙與虛擬航管，使它成為真實飛行訓練強大而廉價的輔助工具——前提是不越過物理與法規的界線。
zh.title: 微軟飛行模擬器真的能教會你開波音737或空中巴士A320嗎？
